own_solution.law: Two-step Doppler in still air: lorry (receding observer) receives f1 = f (v - u_L)/v; lorry re-emits as a source receding from the recorder, recorder moves away from the lorry (with the sound): f2 = f1 (v - u_R)/(v + u_L); shift = f - f2
assumptions: reflection preserves frequency in lorry frame (stated)
recorder on the opposite side of the post from the lorry, so it moves in the direction of the reflected sound

notes: f2/f = (337 x 334)/(343 x 349) = 112558/119707 = 0.9402791; shift = 1500 x 0.0597209 = 89.581 Hz. With the recorder carried at 1.6 m/s relative to the trolley away from the lorry, recorder speed 10.6 m/s: ratio = 337 x 332.4/119707 = 112018.8/119707 = 0.9357749; shift = 96.338 Hz. The 82 m separation affects only the arrival time, not the steady-state Doppler frequency; it appears in no governing relation, so I label it D (one could argue C/no-role; the answer is unchanged either way). Toolbox-carrying and earlier-run sentences have no path to the recorder's frequency. Numbered variants all state 1.6 m/s; TA134 and TA6A4 are numeral-free. Minor idealisation: the technician is assumed to keep walking for as long as the measurement lasts (trolley long enough).
